/entries/e_esteban/desc: One of the twins raised at the convent. He works alongside his brother and is used to thinking of their lives as one.
/entries/e_esteban/archive/0/fields/1/te: To buy the abbess a gift with an advance on his wages, representing his dead brother as well
/entries/e_esteban/archive/0/fields/2/la: The moment he is kept alive
/entries/e_esteban/archive/0/fields/2/te: He falls into crisis before departure; the Captain enters, intervenes and stays with him
/entries/e_esteban/archive/0/fields/3/te: The Captain descends to supervise the cargo. Esteban takes the footbridge and falls when it breaks
/entries/e_manuel/desc: Esteban’s twin, a copyist and laborer, who develops an attachment to an actress he can scarcely put into words.
/entries/e_manuel/archive/0/fields/1/tex: Camila first gives him a powerful attachment and imagined life outside the brothers’ shared existence
/entries/e_manuel/archive/0/fields/2/tex: Seeing his brother’s pain, he stops taking dictation, without thereby erasing every conflict within himself
/entries/e_manuel/archive/0/fields/3/tex: He dies of his worsening knee wound before the bridge collapses; he is not one of its five victims
/entries/e_captain/desc: A quiet, dependable seaman who has travelled many seas. His daughter’s death remains a lasting presence in his life.
/entries/e_captain/archive/0/fields/0/la: The city where he seeks the young man
/entries/e_captain/archive/0/fields/1/te: They once unloaded ships together and respect a silence that neither boasts nor offers excuses
/entries/e_captain/archive/0/fields/2/te: His daughter died long ago; sometimes he still feels that she is only travelling somewhere far away
/entries/e_captain/archive/0/fields/3/te: He offers work, supper and a journey together, without promising that grief will vanish at once
/entries/e_captain/archive/1/fields/1/te: Pio brings him to the night suppers to talk of faraway places and old events with the Viceroy, Archbishop and actress
/entries/e_captain/archive/1/fields/2/te: Pio meets him again while travelling with the child; it is still an ordinary encounter between friends
/entries/e_captain/archive/1/fields/3/te: He takes the river route to supervise cargo, not because he knows the bridge will break
/entries/e_jaime/desc: The son of Camila and the Viceroy, frail and serious. He delights in sunshine and hates others to see his attacks.
/entries/e_jaime/archive/0/fields/1/text: Frail and especially afraid of being watched during an attack, he often tries to hide his distress
/entries/e_jaime/archive/0/fields/2/text: An earlier passage describes him at seven; this does not establish his precise age at the bridge’s collapse
/entries/e_jaime/archive/0/fields/3/text: He appears at the inn after his mother insists on his consent; when the jolting becomes unbearable, Pio carries him
/entries/e_viceroy/desc: The Viceroy of Peru and Camila’s lover, accomplished in courtly manners and troubled by illness, power and weariness.
/entries/e_viceroy/archive/0/fields/1/te: He orders the actress to visit the Marquesa over her public insult, allowing her to keep one pair of shoes
/entries/e_viceroy/archive/0/fields/2/te: He considers aristocratic order and the son-in-law’s influence, while also enjoying humbling the actress
/entries/e_viceroy/archive/0/fields/3/te: Suspecting his lover of seeing other men mixes his authority with emotional insecurity
/entries/e_viceroy/archive/1/fields/1/te: Courtly language and everyday manners give the actress new details for her performances
/entries/e_viceroy/archive/1/fields/2/te: Food, pleasure and long residence abroad bring illness and an enduring weariness
/entries/e_viceroy/archive/1/fields/3/te: He talks with his intimates until dawn, using stories and literature to soothe his homesickness for Spain
/entries/e_archbishop/desc: A high churchman who enjoys language, music and good food, and often finds reasons to postpone action.
/entries/e_juniper/desc: A Franciscan who witnesses the bridge disaster and spends years asking whether the five deaths reveal providence.
/entries/e_juniper/archive/0/fields/1/te: After seeing five people perish, he searches their lives for a design behind the event
/entries/e_juniper/archive/0/fields/2/te: During a plague he compared fifteen victims with fifteen survivors; the results failed to support his expectations
/entries/e_juniper/archive/0/fields/3/te: His record preserves conflicting accounts; it cannot reduce the five people to a ranking of moral worth
